🪜 Upgrade ladders说法升级梯

A nurse who has lived in Canada for ten years tells a colleague, “I think the plan is good, but it is very difficult.” Every word is right, and the sentence still sounds like a learner. One step up the ladder, “I reckon the plan is sound, but it is pretty demanding,” and she sounds like herself. Each ladder below takes one plain word and climbs: everyday → B2 → C1, with the tone each step carries and the moments when the fancier word would backfire.一位在加拿大生活了十年的护士对同事说：「I think the plan is good, but it is very difficult.」每个词都对，听起来却还是学英语的人。往上走一级——「I reckon the plan is sound, but it is pretty demanding」——就像她自己在说话了。下面每架梯子从一个大白话出发往上走：常用 → B2 → C1，写清每一级带什么语气，以及什么时候用了高级词反而坏事。

Levels: CEFR with the CELPIP / CLB band beside it; they correspond only roughly. The dots show formality, from casual to written.级别：CEFR 旁边标思培／CLB 分级，只是大致对应。圆点表示正式度，从口语随意到书面。

think → reckon → believe → would argue → it strikes me that to have an opinion认为；觉得
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 think 认为 neutral中性

🔗 I think so · think it's a good idea

  • I think the bus is faster than the train. 我觉得公交比火车快。
  • Do you think we should call first? 你觉得我们该先打个电话吗？

🎚 Plain and safe in any situation.在任何场合都安全、平实。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 133
  • When I moved from Shanghai to Vancouver, I thought small talk was a waste of time. Why Small Talk Is Not Small
  • There is a meeting I still think about. If I Had Spoken Up
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 reckon 估计；认为（口语） casual口语随意

🔗 I reckon so · reckon it'll rain

  • I reckon we'll be done by four. 我估计我们四点能弄完。
  • She reckons the shop closes early on Sundays. 她估计那家店周日关得早。

🎚 Relaxed and confident; it sounds like a real person guessing, not a learner reporting.随意、笃定，像真人在估计，而不是学生在汇报。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Avoid it in essays, reports and formal emails, where it reads as too chatty.议论文、报告和正式邮件里别用，显得太随便。

B2 · CELPIP 7–8 believe 相信；认为 neutral中性

🔗 firmly believe · I believe that

  • I believe the form has to be signed in person. 我相信这张表格得本人到场签。
  • Many parents believe that homework should start later. 很多家长认为作业应该晚一点开始布置。

🎚 Firmer than think, and slightly more formal; good for a position you can defend.比 think 更坚定、略正式，适合说一个你能为之辩护的立场。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Do not use it for small guesses about facts you could just check: "I believe it's Tuesday" sounds odd unless you are unsure.别用在随手可查的小事上，「I believe it's Tuesday」除非你真不确定，否则听着怪。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 24
  • By the fifth, we had stopped believing the photos. Twelve Viewings and One Lesson
  • The old roof is said to have leaked for at least a decade, and parts of the heating system are believed to date from the original construction. Library Branch to Close for Two Years
C1 · CELPIP 9+ would argue 我会主张（论证语气） formal正式

🔗 I would argue that · one could argue

  • I would argue that the real cost is time, not money. 我认为真正的代价是时间，而不是钱。
  • Some would argue that remote work weakens teams. 有人会说远程办公削弱了团队。

🎚 Signals a reasoned claim you are ready to support with evidence.表示这是一个经过推理、准备拿证据支撑的观点。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Too heavy for everyday chat: "I'd argue this pizza is good" sounds like a joke.日常闲聊里太重，「I'd argue this pizza is good」听起来像在开玩笑。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ it strikes me that 我觉得；我注意到 neutral中性

🔗 it strikes me that · what strikes me is

  • It strikes me that nobody has asked the tenants. 我突然意识到，没人问过租户的意见。
  • It strikes me that the problem started after the update. 我觉得问题是在更新之后才出现的。

🎚 Thoughtful and personal: an observation that has just occurred to you.带思考感、个人化：一个刚刚想到的观察。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Not for firm opinions you have held for years, and not in a numbered list of arguments.不适合说你坚持多年的立场，也别放进一二三条的论点清单里。

✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

I think the new schedule will cause problems. 我觉得新排班会出问题。

  • I reckon the new schedule is going to cause problems.
  • I'd argue that the new schedule will create more problems than it solves.
  • It strikes me that the new schedule could cause problems.

Did your version work as well?你的改写达到这个效果了吗？

say → point out → mention → maintain → remark to put something into words说
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 say 说 neutral中性

🔗 say that · say sorry

  • He said he would call back. 他说会回电话。
  • What did the doctor say? 医生怎么说？

🎚 The default verb for reporting words.转述别人说话的默认动词。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 291
  • At work I said good morning and went straight to my desk. Why Small Talk Is Not Small
  • I said nothing. If I Had Spoken Up
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 point out 指出 neutral中性

🔗 point out that · point out a mistake

  • She pointed out that the price did not include tax. 她指出价格不含税。
  • Thanks for pointing out the error in my email. 谢谢你指出我邮件里的错误。

🎚 Draws attention to a fact others may have missed.提醒别人注意一个可能被忽略的事实。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Not for opinions or feelings; you point out facts, not that you are happy.不用于观点和感受；point out 的对象是事实，不是「我很高兴」。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 21
  • "Could I point out one risk?" "I might be wrong, but the dates do not seem to match." They are soft, and they work. If I Had Spoken Up
  • My colleague pointed out that the client would have to figure out what I meant, and that a misunderstanding now would cost us more later. An Email That Took Three Drafts
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 mention 提到 neutral中性

🔗 mention in passing · briefly mention

  • He mentioned that his sister lives in Calgary. 他提到他姐姐住在卡尔加里。
  • The letter mentions a deadline but no date. 信里提到了截止期，却没写日期。

🎚 Says something briefly, often in passing.简短地、常常是顺带地说一下。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Do not use it for the main message: "She mentioned she was quitting" makes big news sound minor.别用在主要信息上：「She mentioned she was quitting」会把大事说得像小事。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 11
  • Every time I mention care or moving, they change the subject. How Do I Talk to My Parents About the Future?
  • Some entries described conversations with friends; others mentioned the smell of fresh bread or the satisfaction of completing a difficult task. The Art of Contentment
C1 · CELPIP 9+ maintain 坚称 formal正式

🔗 maintain that · maintain one's innocence

  • The landlord maintains that the heater was working. 房东坚称暖气当时是好的。
  • Some researchers maintain that sleep matters as much as diet. 一些研究人员坚持认为睡眠和饮食同样重要。

🎚 Keeps insisting on a claim, often against doubt.在被怀疑的情况下坚持一个说法。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Wrong for a one-off comment; it implies repeated insistence.一次性随口说的话不能用，它暗含反复坚持。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 9
  • It is about maintaining relationships in which individuals can give support and receive it in return. The Science of Connection
  • Of course, nobody can maintain an ideal routine every day. Is Balance Possible?
C1 · CELPIP 9+ remark 评论说；说起 formal正式

🔗 remark on · remark that

  • A neighbour remarked that the street had become much quieter. 一位邻居说起，这条街安静多了。
  • Visitors often remark on how polite drivers are here. 来访者常提到这里的司机多有礼貌。

🎚 A short comment or observation, a little literary.一句简短的评论或观察，略带书面味。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Sounds stiff in casual speech; with friends, just say said or mentioned.日常口语里显得生硬，跟朋友说话用 said 或 mentioned 就好。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 1
  • Under pressure, people tend to see fewer options, interpret neutral remarks as hostile, and cling to their opening position. What Conflict Does to the Brain
✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

She said the meeting was too long. 她说会议太长了。

  • She pointed out that the meeting ran far too long.
  • She maintained that the meeting was much longer than it needed to be.
  • She remarked that the meeting had dragged on.

tell → let … know → keep … posted → notify → brief … on to give someone information告诉
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 tell 告诉 neutral中性

🔗 tell sb about sth · tell the truth

  • Can you tell me where the station is? 你能告诉我车站在哪吗？
  • She told us about the new rules. 她跟我们讲了新规定。

🎚 Plain and correct, but can sound abrupt as a request.平实正确，用来提要求时可能显得生硬。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 112
  • The second surprise is that nobody will tell you the rules that matter. The First Week: What Nobody Tells You
  • They cannot tell if you are friendly or angry." The advice she gave me was simple: every morning, ask one person one question that is not about work. Why Small Talk Is Not Small
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 let … know 告知一声 casual口语随意

🔗 let me know · let sb know in advance

  • Let me know when you get home. 到家了告诉我一声。
  • I'll let the school know that he's sick. 我会告诉学校他病了。

🎚 Friendly and light; the normal way to ask for an update.友好、轻松，请别人告知时最常用。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Too casual for legal or official notices, where the wording must be exact.法律或官方通知里太随便，那种场合措辞要精确。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 6
  • Let me know by Friday. The Week Before the Move
  • Good luck, and let me know how it goes. Dear Alex: The Client Who Wants More
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 keep … posted 随时通报 casual口语随意

🔗 keep me posted · keep everyone posted

  • Keep me posted on the repairs. 维修进展随时告诉我。
  • I'll keep you posted if anything changes. 有什么变化我随时通知你。

🎚 Asks for updates over time, not just once.请对方持续更新，而不只是告诉一次。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Not for one single fact; use it when the situation will keep developing.只有一件事要说时别用；用在事情会持续发展的场合。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ notify 正式通知 formal正式

🔗 notify sb of sth · notify in writing

  • Tenants usually have to notify the landlord in writing. 租户通常要书面通知房东。
  • You will be notified of the decision by email. 决定结果会通过电邮通知你。

🎚 Official and procedural; typical of forms, contracts and agencies.官方、程序化，表格、合同和机构里常见。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Cold between friends: "Notify me when you arrive" sounds like a work order.朋友之间显得冷：「Notify me when you arrive」像下工单。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ brief … on 简要介绍情况 formal正式

🔗 brief sb on sth · fully brief the team

  • The manager briefed the team on the new system. 经理向团队简要介绍了新系统。
  • Can you brief me on what happened at the meeting? 你能跟我简单说说会上发生了什么吗？

🎚 Gives someone the essential facts they need to act.给对方采取行动所需的要点。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Not for gossip or personal news; it belongs to work and planning.不用于闲话和私事，它属于工作与安排。

✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

Please tell me if the time changes. 时间有变请告诉我。

  • Please let me know if the time changes.
  • Please notify me of any change to the time.
  • Could you keep me posted if the time changes?

Did your version work as well?你的改写达到这个效果了吗？

get → obtain → pick up → secure → acquire to come to have something得到；拿到
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 get 得到 casual口语随意

🔗 get a job · get a letter

  • Where did you get that coat? 你那件外套是在哪买的？
  • I got a reply the next day. 第二天我就收到了回复。

🎚 Covers almost anything, which is why it says little.什么都能表达，所以表达的东西也少。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 110
  • I did not get a raise that year. What I Have Learned from Ten Performance Reviews
  • Is there a deposit, and what must happen before you get it back? The Lease Nobody Reads
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 obtain 获得（正式） formal正式

🔗 obtain permission · obtain a copy

  • You can obtain a copy of the form online. 你可以在网上拿到这张表的副本。
  • She obtained permission to work from home. 她获准在家办公。

🎚 Formal and neutral; common in instructions and official writing.正式中性，指示和公文里常见。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Stiff in conversation: "I obtained a coffee" is comic.口语里很生硬：「I obtained a coffee」听着好笑。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 5
  • Scientific knowledge becomes more robust when independent researchers examine similar questions and obtain comparable results. How Does Health Evidence Become Knowledge?
  • It includes understanding legal rights, obtaining reliable advice, finding affordable representation, and having disputes resolved without unreasonable delay. Justice Should Not Depend on Wealth
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 pick up 顺带学会；淘到 casual口语随意

🔗 pick up a few words · pick up a bargain

  • I picked up some French while I was there. 我在那边时顺带学了点法语。
  • You can pick up a cheap desk at a garage sale. 在车库甩卖上能淘到便宜的书桌。

🎚 Getting something easily or by chance.轻松地或偶然地得到。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Wrong when the getting took effort; you do not "pick up" a degree.费了力气得到的不能用，学位不是 pick up 来的。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ secure 争取到 formal正式

🔗 secure funding · secure a place

  • They secured a place for their son at the new school. 他们给儿子在新学校争取到了一个名额。
  • The group finally secured funding for the project. 这个团体终于为项目争取到了资金。

🎚 Getting something valuable after effort or competition.经过努力或竞争得到有价值的东西。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Overblown for small everyday things: you do not secure a parking ticket.用在日常小事上就夸张了。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ acquire 习得；获得 written书面

🔗 acquire skills · acquire a taste for

  • Young children often acquire the sounds of a new language more easily than adults. 小孩子往往比成人更容易掌握新语言的发音。
  • Over time she acquired a taste for strong coffee. 慢慢地她爱上了浓咖啡。

🎚 Gradual gain, or a formal purchase by an organisation.逐渐获得，或机构的正式收购。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Too formal for buying something in a shop.在商店买东西用它太正式。

✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

I got a work permit last year. 我去年拿到了工作许可。

  • I obtained a work permit last year.
  • I managed to secure a work permit last year.

Did your version work as well?你的改写达到这个效果了吗？

get better → improve → pick up → come a long way → take a turn for the better to become better变好
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 get better 变好 casual口语随意

🔗 get better at sth · get much better

  • The weather got better in the afternoon. 下午天气好转了。
  • I'm getting better at cooking. 我做饭越来越好了。

🎚 Natural but vague about how much.自然，但说不清好了多少。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 4
  • After a few weeks, I started to get better at it. A Chat About Free Time
  • But everyone is a beginner once, and people tend to get better at a skill faster than they expect when they practise a little every week. Too Busy for a Hobby?
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 improve 改善 neutral中性

🔗 improve steadily · improve dramatically

  • His health improved after he started walking daily. 他开始每天走路后身体好多了。
  • Service has improved a lot since last year. 跟去年比，服务改进了很多。

🎚 Neutral and works in speech and writing.中性，口语书面都能用。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Fine almost everywhere; only weak when you could say how it improved.几乎哪里都能用；只是在能说清怎么好的时候显得弱。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 23
  • First, life expectancy has risen because of cleaner water, better nutrition, vaccines and improved treatment of heart disease and infection. Why Populations Grow Older
  • A sudden increase may indicate a developing problem, although seasonal changes, improved reporting or changes in testing practices could also explain it. The Evidence Behind a Public Health Alert
B2 · CELPIP 7–8 pick up 回升；好转 casual口语随意

🔗 business picks up · things pick up

  • Sales usually pick up before the holidays. 节前销量通常会回升。
  • Things picked up once the new manager arrived. 新经理来了以后情况好转了。

🎚 After a slow or bad period, activity starts again.在低迷之后重新活跃起来。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Not for a person's skill: "my English picked up" is less clear than "improved".不太用于个人能力，「my English picked up」不如 improved 清楚。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ come a long way 进步很大 neutral中性

🔗 have come a long way · come a long way since

  • Her English has come a long way since she arrived. 来了以后她的英语进步很大。
  • The service has come a long way in two years. 两年里这项服务进步很大。

🎚 Recognises big progress over time, warm and encouraging.肯定一段时间的大进步，温暖、鼓励。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Wrong for short-term change; you cannot come a long way in a day.不用于短期变化，一天之内谈不上 come a long way。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ take a turn for the better 好转；出现转机 neutral中性

🔗 take a turn for the better · take a sudden turn

  • Her condition took a turn for the better overnight. 她的病情一夜之间好转了。
  • The talks took a turn for the better on Friday. 周五谈判出现了转机。

🎚 A clear change of direction in a situation.情况方向上的明显转折。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Too dramatic for small, slow progress like learning words.用在背单词这种慢慢进步上太戏剧化。

✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

My English is getting better. 我的英语在变好。

  • My English is improving steadily.
  • My English has really picked up.
  • My English has come a long way.

help → give … a hand → support → facilitate → be instrumental in to make something easier for someone帮助
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 help 帮助 neutral中性

🔗 help sb do sth · help with sth

  • My neighbour helped me fix the fence. 邻居帮我修了篱笆。
  • This app helps you track spending. 这个应用帮你记账。

🎚 Clear and universal.清楚、通用。

B2 · CELPIP 7–8 give … a hand 搭把手 casual口语随意

🔗 give me a hand · give sb a hand with sth

  • Can you give me a hand with the dishes? 能帮我洗下碗吗？
  • Two friends gave us a hand on moving day. 搬家那天两个朋友来帮了忙。

🎚 Friendly, physical or practical help.友好的、动手的实际帮忙。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Not for abstract help: a policy does not "give a hand" to families.不用于抽象帮助，政策不会 give a hand。

B2 · CELPIP 7–8 support 支持 neutral中性

🔗 support sb through sth · fully support

  • The school supports new families in many ways. 学校在很多方面支持新来的家庭。
  • Her manager supported her through a hard year. 艰难的一年里经理一直支持她。

🎚 Ongoing help over time, practical or emotional.持续的帮助，实际的或情感上的。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Odd for a single small act: "she supported me with the door" is wrong.单次的小动作不能用，「she supported me with the door」是错的。

  • Instead, our first conversations revealed how differently individuals understood health, risk and the availability of support. What Our Community Survey Revealed
C1 · CELPIP 9+ facilitate 促进；使便利 formal正式

🔗 facilitate access · facilitate a discussion

  • The new ramp facilitates access for wheelchair users. 新坡道方便了轮椅使用者进出。
  • A volunteer facilitated the discussion. 一名志愿者主持了讨论。

🎚 Makes a process easier; typical of reports and meetings.让一个过程更顺利，报告和会议里常见。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Jargon-like in normal talk; people help, they rarely "facilitate" a friend.日常说话像行话，帮朋友不说 facilitate。

📖 On this site本站文章原句 1
  • Eventually, both agreed to take part in a carefully facilitated meeting. A Different Kind of Justice
C1 · CELPIP 9+ be instrumental in 起关键作用 formal正式

🔗 be instrumental in doing sth · be instrumental in setting up

  • She was instrumental in setting up the food bank. 她在建立食物银行的过程中起了关键作用。
  • Parents were instrumental in getting the crossing built. 家长们在推动修建人行横道上功不可没。

🎚 Smoothly returns the talk to the main point.把话题顺畅地拉回主线。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Needs a real earlier topic; it is not a sentence opener for anything.前面要有真正的话题，不是随便哪句的开头。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ be that as it may 尽管如此 formal正式

🔗 be that as it may, ... · be that as it may, we still

  • Be that as it may, the rule still applies. 尽管如此，规定仍然适用。
  • The rent is high. Be that as it may, the location is great. 房租很高。即便如此，地段很好。

🎚 Accepts a point but moves past it firmly.承认一点，但坚定地越过它。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Formal and can sound dismissive of the other person's point.很正式，可能显得不重视对方的观点。

✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

Anyway, let's talk about the budget. 总之，我们说说预算吧。

  • Getting back to the budget, ...
  • Be that as it may, the budget still has to be agreed.

Did your version work as well?你的改写达到这个效果了吗？

so yeah → that's about it → so that's why → that, in short, is → that's the long and short of it ending your turn就这样吧
B1 · CELPIP 5–6 so yeah 就这样吧 casual口语随意

🔗 so yeah · yeah, so

  • So yeah, that's why I moved. 嗯，所以我就搬了。
  • So yeah, it was a busy week. 嗯，总之那周挺忙的。

🎚 Very casual ending; common but weak in tests.非常随意的结尾，常见但在考试里弱。

B2 · CELPIP 7–8 that's about it 就这些 casual口语随意

🔗 that's about it · that's it, really

  • That's about it for today. 今天就这些。
  • We cleaned the kitchen, and that's about it. 我们打扫了厨房，就这些。

🎚 Clear signal that you have finished.清楚地表示说完了。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Can sound like you have little to say; add a final point before it.可能显得没什么可说，前面先补一个收尾的点。

B2 · CELPIP 7–8 so that's why 这就是为什么 neutral中性

🔗 so that's why · and that's why

  • So that's why I chose nursing. 这就是我选护理的原因。
  • So that's why we moved to the suburbs. 这就是我们搬到郊区的原因。

🎚 Ends by linking back to the reason.结尾时回扣原因。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Only when you really explained a reason.只在真的解释过原因之后用。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ that, in short, is 简而言之，这就是 formal正式

🔗 that, in short, is · that in a nutshell is

  • That, in short, is why I changed careers. 简而言之，这就是我转行的原因。
  • That, in short, is the plan. 简单说，计划就是这样。

🎚 Polished closing line that sums up.精炼的总结收尾句。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Sounds like a speech; in casual chat it is too polished.像演讲，闲聊里太刻意。

C1 · CELPIP 9+ that's the long and short of it 总而言之 casual口语随意

🔗 that's the long and short of it · the long and short of it is

  • We missed the train, and that's the long and short of it. 我们错过了火车，事情就是这样。
  • The car is too old to fix, and that's the long and short of it. 车太旧修不了了，事情就是这样。

🎚 Idiomatic summing-up, slightly humorous.习语式总结，略带幽默。

⚠️ When not to use it何时不该用 Once per talk at most; it sounds rehearsed if repeated.一次谈话最多一次，重复就像背的。

✍️ Upgrade it升级练习 Rewrite the plain sentence with a B2 or C1 step, then compare.用 B2 或 C1 的说法改写这句，再对照参考答案。

So yeah, that's my plan. 嗯，就是这样，这是我的计划。

  • So that's about it for my plan.
  • That, in short, is my plan.
